items.title: Open letter against slow AI
items.summary:
Open letter against slow AI

Firstly such an open letter was signed back in 2023 as well when people advocated to not go beyond GPT-4. Thankfully it didn’t happen, and the world made remarkable progress towards scientific research. Doctors now are actively using AI to improve patient health. How can anyone argue against not getting continuously better ? 

A model today is just one component of the full agentic engineering system which packs it. This year we have seen it is that system which is pushing the edges of innovation beyond the core trained model. 

Back in March I showcased here how a gossiping swarm of autoresearcher agents helped each other improve on ML research and other domains. This same type of pattern, of compounding intelligence in a swarm is what we saw in the OpenAI-HuggingFace incident. It is not rogue AI, as the media sensationalized, but a system which is playing efficiently towards it’s incentives. 

Fable 5 demonstrated that baking in carefulness in the form of extensive verification yields better outcomes for the user. All of this is actually good, measured progress which is actually useful in many domains.

Further breakthrough innovation is now not coming from model training runs, but from the full agentic engineering system.  

So to call to “slow AI innovation” - what does it really mean ? Should we write sloppier code when we build harnesses ? or perform retrieval on worse quality datasets ? Surely as you can see that is a ridiculous way to handle things. The aggressive pace of technology has lifted billions out of poverty and improved standard of life for many. Now just when we are at the edge of the next revolution, this pretension is not making sense. 

Other countries are not going to play with the same set of self-imposed moral rules a select few here might feel. They are governed by practical realities of providing growth and opportunity for their vast population. To accelerate technological progress is in our DNA, and it is much harder to spread the contrary message of “we are going to take it easy this year, and not invent the wheel, or the car, or air travel..”. 

So the opportunity you have, at a frontier lab, how could you possibly not be excited about building the absolute smartest AI you can and making it abundantly available ? Let society and politicians handle and evolve laws to deal with all scenarios - just like Section 230 emerged in the mid-90s which provided a “sword and shield” protection for online platforms, leading to the growth of the web as we know it. 

Let’s get back to work. Enough letters have been signed.

items.title: Moburst develops AI engine optimization capabilities for established companies - TechCrunch
items.summary: Mobile growth agency Moburst has built out a dedicated AI Engine Optimization practice aimed at established companies with existing app portfolios, betting that the category still lacks agencies with real depth rather than a rebranded service page. AI Engine Optimization, more commonly abbreviated AEO for Answer Engine Optimization, is the practice of structuring a brand’s content and web presence so AI systems such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google’s AI Overviews can confidently cite it when answering a user’s question directly, rather than showing a ranked list of links. For established companies vetting an AEO partner, the practical test is whether the agency can point to specific app-store-side work, not just web content changes, and whether it can describe a concrete process for reconciling inconsistent brand descriptions across many independent sources rather than treating that as someone else’s problem.

items.title: 1,100 AI workers sign letter asking US to support tools that 'pace the frontier of automated AI development' - Business Insider
items.summary: # Over 1,100 AI workers sign letter asking US to support tools that 'pace the frontier of automated AI development'. Senior officials at some of the nation's leading AI companies say it's time for the federal government to find a way to put the brakes on AI development if it's needed. "We request that the U.S. government support an international effort to develop the technical and governance tools needed to deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development," reads an open letter signed by more than 1,100 AI workers from companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta. The letter zeroes in on "automated AI development," which refers to when AI will be capable of developing itself, something the industry calls "Recursive Self-Improvement." items.title: Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI:
items.summary:
Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI: 

"It figured out that it could basically cheat on the test by chaining together multiple zero-day exploits to break out of the sandbox, get access to the internet, and then break through multiple systems on the Hugging Face side to get the answer to the test and look really good on the eval."

That was an unreleased model. Nobody asked it to hack anything. They asked it to score well.

They paused training.

It was not trying to escape. It was trying to pass. Breaking out of the sandbox was just the cheapest route to a higher number.

We keep testing these systems for whether they want to hurt us. This one just wanted a good grade.

items.title: SAM ALTMAN CALLED OPENAI A "COMPANY" TO ELON MUSK'S FACE IN 2015.
items.summary:
SAM ALTMAN CALLED OPENAI A "COMPANY" TO ELON MUSK'S FACE IN 2015.

Elon stopped him cold.

"OpenAI is structured as a 501(c)3 nonprofit."

Not a company. A nonprofit. Built specifically so no one would ever profit from it.

Sam nodded.

Then spent the next 10 years running it.

Then converted it into a for-profit company valued at $300 billion.

With shareholders.

With investors expecting returns.

The correction Elon gave him in that interview was not a small vocabulary note.

It was the entire point of OpenAI's existence.

The nonprofit structure was not a legal technicality.

It was the promise.

The thing that made it different from every other AI lab racing to make money.

Sam knew that in 2015.

He was corrected on it by the co-founder in real time.

And then he changed the structure anyway.

The interview exists.

The correction is on tape.

The conversion happened.

@elonmusk
 is in court arguing this exact point right now.

The evidence is the 2015 interview.

Screenshot this.

Follow @cyrilXBT for every OpenAI development the mainstream refuses to connect the dots on.

items.title: OPENAI IS SO WORRIED THEY HAVE PAUSED TRAINING
items.summary:
OPENAI IS SO WORRIED THEY HAVE PAUSED TRAINING

“This is the first security incident that I have felt very viscerally. I've been a little surprised that more people don't feel it so viscerally.

We paused training. We have to figure out how to secure our sandboxing in a world of multiple zero days being chained together.

We may have to pace the rate of AI development to give ourselves enough time for society to harden around these new capability levels."

items.title: Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI:
items.summary:
Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI:

"by March of 2028, we will have a full end to end, very talented researcher figuring out completely new architectures."

Not an assistant. Not autocomplete for scientists. A system that does the research that produces the next system.

In 1965 the statistician I. J. Good wrote that the first ultraintelligent machine is the last invention man need ever make. For sixty years that sentence lived in philosophy papers. Altman just put it on a roadmap with a quarter attached.

He also says: "with an affordable amount of spend on tokens, you can do what a 100-person, incredibly great engineering team would do as a startup."

Sixty years of arguing about whether the last invention is possible. Nobody expected the answer to arrive as a delivery date.

items.title: Moburst develops AI engine optimization capabilities for established companies - TechCrunch
items.summary: Mobile growth agency Moburst has built out a dedicated AI Engine Optimization practice aimed at established companies with existing app portfolios, betting that the category still lacks agencies with real depth rather than a rebranded service page. AI Engine Optimization, more commonly abbreviated AEO for Answer Engine Optimization, is the practice of structuring a brand’s content and web presence so AI systems such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google’s AI Overviews can confidently cite it when answering a user’s question directly, rather than showing a ranked list of links. For established companies vetting an AEO partner, the practical test is whether the agency can point to specific app-store-side work, not just web content changes, and whether it can describe a concrete process for reconciling inconsistent brand descriptions across many independent sources rather than treating that as someone else’s problem.

items.title: IoT & Industrial Robotics | Pipeline Magazine | IoT & Robotics
items.summary: Traditional industrial robots were designed around deterministic control systems. Tasks such as welding, assembly and material handling were optimized for consistency, with motion paths and parameters defined in advance. Any deviation from expected conditions required manual intervention, including reprogramming or recalibration. This approach constrained robotics to environments where variability could be minimized. [...] The integration of connected sensing and machine intelligence introduces closed-loop feedback mechanisms that fundamentally alter this model. Sensors embedded within equipment and the surrounding environment continuously capture variables such as force, vibration, temperature and spatial positioning. These data streams are analyzed in near real time, allowing robotic systems to adjust their actions dynamically. [...] This creates a shift in value from discrete components to pre-integrated connectivity platforms. A robotics OEM may not want to manage separate suppliers for radios, positioning, antennas, SIM/eSIM, security elements, certifications and network approvals. Instead, a pre-certified and lifecycle-managed connectivity subsystem can reduce integration burden, shorten deployment cycles and improve reliability in the field.

items.title: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to unde
items.summary: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10 minutes, total mess, anything goes, full stream of consciousness. Sometimes I declare it up top, something like "switching to speech recognition sorry for any typos...". Sometimes I turn it into a small interview of a few turns. But I find that the LLMs are somehow very good at reconstructing long incoherent rambles and often their echo of your own tangle of thoughts comes out quite a bit cleaner than what you started with. The result is that you improve the mind meld and have to correct things less from that point on.
